prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the exact same startup race in post_writer(): the task group spawns post_writer as a background task, but nothing signals when it has actually reached `async for session_message in write_stream_reader`. members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Both patch the exact same startup race in post_writer(): the task group spawns post_writer as a background task, but nothing signals when it has actually reached `async for session_message in write_stream_reader`. If the caller proceeds to yield the read/write streams before that point, the first write can race the writer's setup. Both PRs fix it identically — adding `TaskStatus` to the import, adding a `*, task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` kwarg to post_writer, and calling `task_status.started(None)` as the first line inside the context manager so the spawn site can `await tg.start(...)` instead of `tg.start_soon(...)`.

clusters.pick_reason: As submitted, #2555 is the only one of the two whose diff includes updated test coverage (tests/shared/test_exceptions.py) exercising the exact pickle round-trip regression, and it explicitly references and closes the tracked issue (#2431) with a docstring reproducing the precise TypeError. #2478's diff (as shown) touches only exceptions.py with no accompanying test changes — it adds a module-level `_restore_mcp_error` dispatcher with a hardcoded special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError, which is a broader generic mechanism but is unverified here by any new test, and pushes future subclasses needing custom reconstruction into growing an if/else chain rather than each subclass owning its own `__reduce__`. #2555's fix also reconstructs directly from the object's own typed fields (_elicitations, message) rather than round-tripping through the wire-format ErrorData, avoiding the extra indirection layer #2478 introduces. Recommend closing #2478 in favor of #2555; if the generic base-class dispatch in #2478 is still wanted for other MCPError subclasses, it should be filed as a separate follow-up rather than merged as a competing fix for the same bug.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Both patch the exact same startup race in post_writer(): the task group spawns post_writer as a background task, but nothing signals when it has actually reached `async for session_message in write_stream_reader`. If the caller proceeds to yield the read/write streams before that point, the first write can race the writer's setup. Both PRs fix it identically — adding `TaskStatus` to the import, adding a `*, task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` kwarg to post_writer, and calling `task_status.started(None)` as the first line inside the context manager so the spawn site can `await tg.start(...)` instead of `tg.start_soon(...)`.

clusters.pick_reason: #2654 is branched from the current create_context_streams-based implementation and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the actual blocking scenario and verifies the fix; it also resolves the problem by default for all callers with a single hardcoded buffer slot. #2215 is branched off an older pre-refactor version of stdio.py (still calling anyio.create_memory_object_stream directly) and only exposes buffer sizes as opt-in constructor params defaulting to 0, so it doesn't fix the underlying blocking behavior unless a caller explicitly opts in, and would need rebasing onto the newer create_context_streams API to even apply cleanly.

clusters.pick_reason: As submitted, #2555 is the only one of the two whose diff includes updated test coverage (tests/shared/test_exceptions.py) exercising the exact pickle round-trip regression, and it explicitly references and closes the tracked issue (#2431) with a docstring reproducing the precise TypeError. #2478's diff (as shown) touches only exceptions.py with no accompanying test changes — it adds a module-level `_restore_mcp_error` dispatcher with a hardcoded special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError, which is a broader generic mechanism but is unverified here by any new test, and pushes future subclasses needing custom reconstruction into growing an if/else chain rather than each subclass owning its own `__reduce__`. #2555's fix also reconstructs directly from the object's own typed fields (_elicitations, message) rather than round-tripping through the wire-format ErrorData, avoiding the extra indirection layer #2478 introduces. Recommend closing #2478 in favor of #2555; if the generic base-class dispatch in #2478 is still wanted for other MCPError subclasses, it should be filed as a separate follow-up rather than merged as a competing fix for the same bug.
